For \(N=365\), \(\mathbb P(T_N>m)\) is the probability that no two
members of a group of \(m\) people share a birthday, all birthdays
being taken as equally likely; the source reports its approximation as
\(2\%\) smaller than the true probability \(0.524\)
\cite[p.~117]{DurrettPTEAuthor2019}, and
\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-004-birthday-error} proves that the shortfall
lies between \(1.71\) and \(1.74\) percent of the exact value.

Durrett writes \(P(Y_n=y)\) for this density, a convention he keeps
in what follows \cite[p.~118]{DurrettPTEAuthor2019}; here that symbol
keeps its meaning as the probability of the event \(\{Y_n=y\}\), which
is zero for every \(y\)
(\cref{def:p15-w02c-p15-004-density-notation,thm:p15-w02c-p15-004-density-reading}).
